S7. Legal decisions (RQ4)

October 10, 2026
Emma Marshall, J.D., M.A.
University of Nebraska-Lincoln

Probable-cause rulings (H5a, H5b, E4a, E4b)

Table S7.1

Additional probable-cause comparisons: NCM − None and SMA − NCM from the basic model (E4a) and the stereotypical − non-stereotypical difference of the remaining SMA − NCM difference (E4b)

Comparison Letter Predicted direction Δp 95% percentile CI Usable attempts Decision
Note. Δp = difference in the average predicted probability of a yes ruling, primary sample, adjusted. E4a reuses the H5a model and its eligible participants from all six conditions in their own evidence condition, with no directional prediction. E4b reuses the H5b model: each included SMA and NCM participant is predicted under both outcomes and both evidence conditions with their other predictors unchanged, and the non-stereotypical SMA − NCM difference is subtracted from the stereotypical one before averaging. 95% CI = participant percentile bootstrap interval from the same attempts as H5a and H5b. Percentile bootstrap: 10000 within-condition participant resamples; usable attempts per quantity: 10000 of 10000 (failed attempts are not replaced). Decision: each letter's registered rule applied to its saved interval. N = 320 (Stereotypical, None, n = 55; Stereotypical, SMA, n = 52; Stereotypical, NCM, n = 60; Non-stereotypical, None, n = 52; Non-stereotypical, SMA, n = 50; Non-stereotypical, NCM, n = 51).

Stereotypical Non-stereotypical Across evidence conditions
Pathway Letter b 95% CI b 95% CI b 95% CI
Note. b = unstandardized estimate on the probit scale of the ruling's latent response (WLSMV, theta parameterization: that response's intercept is fixed at zero and its residual variance at one, with a separate threshold in each condition), primary sample, adjusted. Serial product = the SMA or NCM − None difference in the relevance or incrimination factor intercept, times that factor's likelihood slope, times the likelihood-to-ruling slope; the two factor-to-likelihood slopes and the likelihood-to-ruling slope are common to the six conditions, and the foreseeability-to-ruling slope differs by outcome and is equal across evidence conditions, as registered. Foreseeability contribution = the outcome − None difference in model-implied foreseeability at the pooled attitude means, times that outcome's foreseeability-to-ruling slope; the consistency contrast (E4h) is the mean of the two outcome-consistent contributions (stereotypical SMA, non-stereotypical NCM) minus the mean of the two inconsistent ones. 95% CI = participant percentile bootstrap interval for every row, the foreseeability coefficients included (decided on 2026-09-24). Percentile bootstrap: 10000 within-condition participant resamples; usable attempts per quantity: 882 of 10000 (failed attempts are not replaced). Only 882 of 10,000 resamples produced a usable fit (the others did not converge or failed the admissibility checks); the interval summarizes those resamples alone, so it is wide and I do not interpret it. Letter = the registered read; the other rows are reported without a support gate. Scaled fit of the adjusted model: scaled χ²(2088) = 2405.87, p < .001, CFI = 0.585, TLI = 0.699, RMSEA = 0.054 (90% CI [0.043, 0.064]), SRMR = 0.176. No auxiliary items: the registered categorical model uses complete responses (registered analysis supplement). Decision: each letter's registered rule applied to its saved interval. Follow-up with average scores (not preregistered): serial products, foreseeability coefficients and the consistency contrast on the probit scale, primary sample

Adjusted: bootstrap 95% CI Adjusted: Bayesian 95% credible interval Unadjusted: bootstrap 95% CI Unadjusted: Bayesian 95% credible interval
Pathway Letter b 95% CI Median 95% CrI b 95% CI Median 95% CrI
Note. This follow-up with average scores is not preregistered and decides nothing; no decision rule is applied to it. Relevance and incrimination = the mean of each participant's ten ratings (the registered H2a fallback's scoring); likelihood = abortion likelihood (0–100); foreseeability = the registered four-item mean; ruling = the probable-cause ruling. One model for all six conditions (a condition factor, no common intercept): least-squares regressions of relevance, incrimination and foreseeability on the conditions and of likelihood on the conditions, relevance and incrimination, and a probit regression of the ruling on the conditions, likelihood and one foreseeability slope for each outcome condition. Adjusted: the four attitudes in every equation and error preference in the ruling; unadjusted: neither. Same eligible participants (complete responses) as the registered model; each quantity is computed from these coefficients as the registered model computes it from its own (probit scale). Letter marks the registered question a row answers in the registered model. b and 95% CI = the estimate and its participant percentile bootstrap interval over 10,000 participant resamples, the resample sets of the registered model (failed attempts are not replaced). Usable resamples per quantity: adjusted 10,000 of 10,000 (none failed); unadjusted 10,000 of 10,000 (none failed). Median and 95% CrI = the posterior median and the 95% equal-tailed credible interval of each quantity from the same model fitted with brms (Stan through cmdstanr) as one multivariate model (four Gaussian equations and the probit ruling, no residual correlations): 4 chains of 2,000 iterations (1,000 warm-up), seed 4747, continuous variables centered at their means. Priors, one rule for every version: normal(0, 2.5 × the outcome's SD) on each coefficient of the four Gaussian equations and student_t(3, 0, 2.5 × that SD) on their residual SDs; normal(0, 1) on each probit coefficient. Diagnostics (criteria: every R-hat ≤ 1.01, bulk and tail ESS ≥ 400, no divergent transitions): adjusted largest R-hat 1.014, smallest bulk and tail ESS 1,235 and 470, 0 divergent (criteria not met: not interpreted); unadjusted largest R-hat 1.003, smallest bulk and tail ESS 3,364 and 2,635, 0 divergent (criteria met). A version that fails them is shown and not interpreted. Doubling every prior scale changed the primary adjusted medians by at most 0.011 and any median or interval bound by at most 0.047 (probit scale).
